habitat: Fringes of lagoons, floodplains and dams, less often rivers. Single birds or groups, sometimes large flocks. Nomadic.
summary: A dark egret with uniform colouring, dark eyes, dark legs and bright yellow feet. It forms a canopy with its wings when fishing. Newman calls it an uncommon to locally common resident.

similar.note: Little Egret is white, with a black bill, black legs and yellow feet. Black Heron is uniformly dark, with the same yellow feet, and spreads its wings into a fishing canopy.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 4–16.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Dark eyes, dark legs and bright yellow feet. The body colour is uniform.

wings.pattern: The wings are spread into a canopy while fishing.

viewNotes.note: Uniformly dark, with yellow feet. One or both wings may be held as a fishing canopy.
Dark face and a dark eye.
Dark back. The canopy is the usual open-wing view.
Dark above when the canopy is raised.
Dark from below. A separate underwing colour was not named.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The texts do not separate the sexes. The catalogue cut is not labelled by sex. Grade A from Doubounoro, Chad.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it an uncommon to locally common resident and also nomadic. Chick down is not described. The call is grade A from Chad.
